facts.old: A RAG system fails in two places: retriever did not put the right text in the prompt, or generator had it and answered badly; an end-to-end score cannot tell them apart
Measure the two halves separately, then end to end
Retrieval half: classical IR metrics, cheap, deterministic, reproducible given labels
Generation half: LLM judge reads question, context, answer; needs no chunk labels; inherits judge failure modes (variance, bias, drift)
End to end: small human-labelled golden set plus failure bucketing
The one idea: for every wrong answer first ask whether the gold chunk was in the prompt

facts.old: Golden sets: a few hundred beat ten thousand synthetic
Step 1 mine real queries; synthetic over-represents clean questions
Step 2 label relevant chunk IDs and reference answer; SME time is the bottleneck
Step 3 synthetic generation to bootstrap, then human-filter; unfiltered are easy because they quote the chunk
Step 4 hard negatives: unanswerable, multi-hop, ambiguous, near-duplicates
Step 5 version, re-label on corpus change, never tune on held-out
Golden set promotion, CI gates, label-noise audit on Production eval engineering
